name: Age Of Accountability
overview: The concept of the Age of Accountability in Scripture is reflected in the distinction between those who are considered responsible for their actions and those who are not yet capable of discerning good from evil. For example, in Exodus 30:14, individuals twenty years and older are counted for offerings, indicating a recognition of maturity and responsibility. Deuteronomy 1:39 highlights that children who lack knowledge of good and evil are not held accountable in the same way and are granted inheritance. Proverbs 20:11 further confirms that even children are known by their deeds, implying an awareness of moral behavior begins at a certain stage. These passages collectively suggest that accountability before God is linked to an age or level of understanding where one can differentiate right from wrong.
